semantic_findings: Capacity is a logical entry count clamped to at least1; index construction does not reserve that capacity. A miss trims at >= before constructing the new value; frame end trims only at > and preserves unused resident entries.

begin_frame replaces the report with externally supplied frame label and current resident/peak, retaining index/LRU. clear releases owned entries and resets current estimate while preserving prior peak and accumulating clear/eviction counters.

Full text and stable K identity select an entry. Explicit insertion updates V/estimate while retaining old K/Arc and touching LRU. contains_exact does not touch or increment query counters; only final absence records collision/width misses.
Layout insertion identity compares the complete stored validity value; reading asks that validity to contain the query width. A lazy hit keeps the old validity/value and does not invoke FnOnce.

Exact validity normalizes signed zero but otherwise preserves float bits, including nonfinite patterns. Range storage does not certify order or layout invariance; contains requires finite endpoints/query and a half-open condition.

Returned V/Arc references borrow the cache. A caller must explicitly own/clone resources to outlive that borrow or cache eviction. Generic V has no automatic Ready/geometry/font-generation authentication; UI owns those gates.

Estimated bytes include entry representation, text length and explicitly reported extra heap; they exclude container capacities, Arc header/sharing and unreported allocations. Counters are logical telemetry, not allocator/RSS or physical constant-time acceptance.
Lazy miss accounts/trims before invoking caller code, with no Result rollback or panic-recovery contract. No new BUG is inferred merely from that documented sequence.
